context: (A) Require both catalog facts (partition_key AND sort_key) -- or a separate partition-key intent -- before the generic corroborator upgrades a combined PARTITION BY/ORDER BY table to applied_verified. (B) Record the tuned ORDER BY DDL at connection.execute(optimized) so applied_ledger_hash orders the CREATE TABLE before the later OPTIMIZE TABLE, instead of queuing it in _applied_layout_operations. Land only in the conservative direction: never over-certify. Confirm on a live ClickHouse run per issue #1293.
description: Two validated/reproduced reviewer findings on this batch's #1275 (tuning-verification-footprint-duckdb-clickhouse), still live at develop 14b0271c in benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/workload.py; deferred by the maintainer to GitHub issue #1293 (needs a real ClickHouse run to confirm) and NOT yet in the tracker. (A) PR #1275 discussion_r3638089585 (workload.py ~224): a combined PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY CREATE TABLE is recorded only as sort_key, so the generic corroborator can reach applied_verified without ever matching the configured partition_key. (B) PR #1275 discussion_r3638089592 (workload.py ~219): tuned ORDER BY DDL is queued in _applied_layout_operations and folded only after data validation, so applied_ledger_hash orders a later OPTIMIZE TABLE before the earlier CREATE TABLE. SOUNDNESS-relevant (applied_verified certification + ledger-hash input ordering) -> its own PR will not auto-merge under CODEOWNERS.
